auth.title: Sign in
auth.subtitle: Your agents keep running while you're away.
auth.keepSignedIn: Keep me signed in on this device
auth.inviteOnly: No account? Blackhouse is invite-only per workspace — ask an admin to add you from Members.
auth.pitchHeadline: Persistent coding agents, each in its own sandbox, sharing your channels.

agents.title: Roster
agents.description: Every agent in this workspace, its container state and what it is doing. Mentioning one in a channel injects the prompt into its live terminal.
agents.stopBody: @{{handle}} stops mid-task. Its workspace and state volumes survive, so starting it again resumes from where it left off — but the live terminal session is lost.
agents.destroyBody: @{{handle}} and its container are removed for good. The handle becomes available again. This cannot be undone.

createAgent.title: New agent
createAgent.blueprintBlurb: A blueprint bundles the CLI, base image, system prompt, skills, MCP servers, and default sandbox & egress policy. You can override everything in the next step.
createAgent.noBlueprintsBody: An admin needs to create one in Settings → Blueprints before an agent can be spawned.
createAgent.handleInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits, - and _ only; 2–32 characters.
createAgent.repoHelp: Cloned into the agent's own workspace volume.
createAgent.repoInvalid: Enter an https:// or git@ URL
createAgent.budgetHelp: The agent pauses when it hits the cap — container and terminal stay up, new runs are refused.

blueprints.title: Blueprints
blueprints.description: Reusable agent definitions — CLI, base image, system prompt, skills, MCP servers, and default sandbox & egress. Spawning an agent starts from one of these.
blueprints.dialogDescription: The CLI is also the sidecar adapter key: it decides how this agent's transcript is read back into a channel.
blueprints.name: Name
blueprints.cliHelp: Picks the sidecar adapter. Anything other than Claude Code degrades to a PTY scrape.
blueprints.agentCommandHelp: Exec'd directly, never through a shell — container-exit must mean agent-exit.
blueprints.dockerfileHelp: Leave empty to use a prebuilt image. Editing this resets the build status.
blueprints.buildLogDescription: Output from the last image build of "{{name}}".
blueprints.deleteBody: "{{name}}" is removed. Agents already created from it keep running; new agents can no longer be spawned from it.
blueprints.egressPolicyHelp: What an agent from this blueprint may reach. Binding only while enforcement is on in Settings → Egress.

policy.open: Open — any host this machine can reach

blueprints.egressOpenWarning: Open ignores the allowlist entirely: model-authored code reaches any host this machine can.
blueprints.egressAllowlistHelp: Seeds the rule table the first time an agent from this blueprint starts. After that the rules are authoritative — edit them in Settings → Egress.
blueprints.egressAllowlistEmpty: No hosts. An agent from this blueprint starts with only the workspace rules.
blueprints.servicesHelp: Each of these starts a real service inside the sandbox next to the CLI. One agent running both took a 2-CPU host to load average 27, so a small host cannot run many of them. Off unless an agent is expected to use the tab.
blueprints.enableIdeHelp: Runs code-server — a full VS Code server — for the agent's IDE tab.
blueprints.enableBrowserHelp: Runs node, Playwright and a Chromium for the agent's browser tab.

runtimes.title: Sandbox runtimes
runtimes.description: What this host can actually run. A blueprint asking for a runtime this host lacks falls back to the strongest one detected — quietly, which is why this page exists.
runtimes.detectFailed: Could not reach the container daemon

notes.runc: The OCI default. Namespace isolation only — the agent shares the host kernel.
notes.runsc: gVisor. A user-space kernel between the agent and the host, and the intended default on Linux. Absent on macOS and on Podman.
notes.kata: A real VM boundary per container. Needs nested virtualization and /dev/kvm. Detection only — the driver is a documented stub.

egress.title: Egress allowlist
egress.description: Whether an agent's policy is binding, and the hosts it may reach.
egress.enforceAdminOnly: Only an admin can change enforcement.
egress.envOverride: BLACKHOUSE_EGRESS_ENFORCE is set and wins over this setting. The change was saved but is not in force; unset the variable to control enforcement from here.

stateBody.enforced: Agents run on an internal network and reach the internet only through their egress proxy — a host that is not listed below is refused at connect time. The proxy also resolves names on the agent's behalf, so an allowlisted host resolves no matter what the sandbox's own resolver can reach.
stateBody.ineffective: The switch is on and nothing is being enforced. Agents keep the ordinary bridge network, which means this instance has the isolation someone believes in but does not have.
stateBody.off: Not enforced yet. A blueprint that says allowlist is decorative — agents keep the ordinary bridge network and reach whatever this host can.

reason.policy-open: The policy is open, and open never consults an allowlist.
reason.host-mode: BLACKHOUSE_NETWORK is unset, so agents run on the host's default network and cannot be moved behind a proxy.
reason.unroutable-harness-url: BLACKHOUSE_CONTAINER_URL resolves to {{host}}, which an agent on an internal network cannot reach. Point it at an address that works from inside the container network.
reason.no-token: No proxy token could be derived, because BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is unset.

egress.rulesApplyNote: Rules are resolved when an agent starts. Restart an agent for a change here to reach it — editing this list does not widen what a running agent can already do.
egress.workspaceScopeHelp: Granted to every agent, whichever blueprint it came from.
egress.addToWorkspace: Add a host for every agent
egress.emptyWorkspace: No workspace-wide hosts. Under enforcement an agent reaches only what its own blueprint grants.
egress.blueprintScopeHelp: Granted to agents created from this blueprint, on top of the workspace rules.
egress.emptyBlueprint: No hosts of its own. Under enforcement an agent from this blueprint reaches only the workspace rules.
egress.agentScopeHelp: Added for one agent. They can be revoked here; granting one belongs on the agent itself.
egress.policyOpenNote: Policy is open: no allowlist is consulted and agents reach any host this machine can. Change it in Blueprints.
egress.policyNoneNote: Policy is none: agents get no egress at all, and these rules are never read.
egress.pendingDefaults: {{count}} host from this blueprint's default list has not been copied in yet, so it grants nothing: {{hosts}}
egress.pendingDefaults_other: {{count}} hosts from this blueprint's default list have not been copied in yet, so they grant nothing: {{hosts}}
egress.hostHelp: example.com · .example.com for subdomains · example.com:8443 for another port · example.com:* for any port
egress.invalidHost: Enter one host with no spaces — api.anthropic.com, .github.com, or registry.npmjs.org:443.
egress.duplicateHost: That host is already listed here.
egress.confirmOnBody: Agents will start behind a CONNECT proxy and reach only the hosts listed here. Anything missing fails at connect time.
egress.confirmOnDetail: Agents already running keep the network they started on and pick this up the next time they start. The proxy is also what resolves names for a gVisor sandbox, so enforcement is what gives those agents working DNS.
egress.confirmOffBody: Agents go back to the ordinary bridge network and reach whatever this host can, whatever their blueprint's policy says.
egress.confirmOffDetail: The rules stay listed and nothing checks them. New agents get no proxy, so a gVisor sandbox loses its name resolution along with the restriction.

members.title: Members
members.description: People and agents in this workspace. Only humans can approve an agent→agent dispatch.
members.addDescription: Creates the account directly with a starting password. There is no email invite yet.
members.name: Name
members.passwordHelp: Share it out of band. They can change it from Profile.
members.removeBody: {{name}} loses access immediately. Agents they created keep running.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Your own account on this Blackhouse instance.
profile.displayNameHelp: Shown beside your messages in channels.
profile.changePasswordHelp: Changing it does not sign out your other sessions.
profile.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match

result.confirmDelete: This artifact is removed from the channel. This cannot be undone.

browser.noWebCodecs: This browser has no WebCodecs support, so the remote screen cannot be decoded.
